metadata.title: Claimed and Measured: Gyro-S v2 on Real Coding Tasks, and Why the Test Needs Testing Too
metadata.description:
A model announcement claims 18% less drift on held-out text, 27% less on tool calls and 14% less on code for Gyro-S v2. This report runs the same bench as report 5 - 20 questions, 40 easy and 40 hard graded function tasks, and five replayed real repository fixes judged by hidden tests - on Gyro-S v2 alone and in parallel with Signal 2, against Signal 2's own reference runs. Alone it passes 8/20, 37/40, 8/40 and 3 of 5 real tasks; beside Signal 2, 15/20, 35/40, 32/40 and 2 of 5.

Its failures are behavioural: early stops with missing answers (28 of 40 hard answers missing), announcing a step and ending the turn without doing it (7 guard hits alone), and identical-write loops (14 guard hits in the dual run). A model-specific workaround - raising the announced-no-action cap from 2 to 6 for Gyro-S only - coincides with the jump from 8/40 to 32/40, so that gain is confounded.

Two instrument faults of the same night would have produced wrong verdicts: a provider registered disabled was logged as done with 1-second walls and 0 passes (Gyro-S would have scored 0%), and a real task rewrote the bench's shared config so the next two tasks were refused in 1 second (a code-graph off arm would have read 3/5). Both were found and fixed: the bench now resolves the provider before the series, records refused starts as errors, and rewrites its own config before every task.

With one run per cell and a spread of 8/20 against 15/20 on the same short set, no ranking of the two models follows; the operational choice is that Signal 2 stays the local worker and the Gyro-S v2 runtime is stopped. A real test only counts once the test itself has been verified.

Version 0.2 corrects the description of the PLE table.

Sixth report of the PAI Reports series. Sources: https://github.com/mnott/PAI-Reports
